1. Which public offices (elected and appointed) have you held? (Include dates of service).
2. Have you ever been endorsed by AFSCME or AFL-CIO COPE? If so, for what offices?
3. Have you ever been turned down by AFSCME for an endorsement?
4. Are you or have you been a union member? To which union(s) do you or did you belong? Please indicate which years.
5. What was your level of participation in your union?
6. Briefly describe your work background.
7. Briefly describe your educational background.
8. To what fraternal, professional, civic or social organizations do you belong
9. What is your fundraising goal? How much have you raised to date? Current cash on hand?
10. What is your plan to win?
11. Describe your goals and priorities for this office?
12. What do you think is the biggest challenge facing the elected body you seek to serve on?
13. Please give examples of how you have worked with public sector unions on policy issues and/or budgets in the past.

14. As an elected official, the Brown Act allows you to be accessible to workers and their representatives on work-related issues, including the negotiation process. What steps will you take to be accessible to workers and their representatives, and if need be, to act as a facilitator if negotiations reach an impasse?

15. Please check which actions you would be willing to undertake: Sign a letter of support to public workers / Personally speak to an employer during difficult contract negotiations / Speak at a public forum on the right to organize / Speak at a public forum about the right of public sector workers to determine wages and benefits through the collective bargaining process
16. Have you ever crossed a picket line? In what cases would you do so?
17. What would an endorsement from AFSCME mean to you?
18. Do you support public workers’ rights to collectively bargain wages, benefits, and working conditions? Please discuss the steps you have taken to support these rights in the past.
19. Do you support the right of public employees to strike?

20. Do you support employer-paid medical, vision, dental, and retiree medical plans for public employees, including part timers, temporary and seasonal workers? At what level of employment do you think coverage should begin?

21. During an economic crisis, many public employees do their part by foregoing raises and COLAs, taking pay reductions, increasing co-payments and employee contributions, agreeing to furloughs, and doing more work as positions are left unfilled. If employees make sacrifices for the fiscal health of their agency during hard times, do you support making them whole for whatever concessions they gave during the crisis?

22. Middle income and low wage public employees continue to see their paychecks shrink due to stagnant wages, reduced hours and increased medical and retirement contributions, meanwhile, the compensation for those at the top is growing. Do you believe that benefit and wage increases offered to management, fire, and safety also be offered to rank and file union members?
23. In what instances do you support the outsourcing (privatization) of public services?
24. Do you support insourcing? When?

25. What is your position on using permanent temporary workers? Should part-time workers, seasonal workers, and temporary workers in the public sector be afforded the same rights as are permanent employees?

questions.section: Public Health, Worker Safety and Continuity of Employment
questions.question: 26. If elected, what will you do to ensure worker safety and continuity of employment as a result of public health crises, including heat waves, wildfires and unsafe air quality?

questions.section: Racial and Gender Equity in the Workforce
questions.question: 27. How do you define equity?

questions.section: Racial and Gender Equity in the Workforce
questions.question: 28. If elected, what will you do to work towards racial and gender equity in the workplace?
29. Do you think climate change is an important issue? What types of programs or legislation do you think are needed to address climate change?
30. What is your position on Charter Schools? Do you believe that public funds should be spent on Charter Schools?

31. As elected officials, it is incumbent upon you to develop the next generation of leaders. What type of work have you done in this area and what will you do when you take office to ensure we are developing the next generation?
32. If you receive our endorsement, are you requesting a donation? If so, what amount are you looking for?

org_research:
AFSCME Council 57 — 2026 Election Cycle Candidate Questionnaire. Transcribed from the fillable PDF text layer, verbatim. Council 57 is the parent body of Public Employees Union Local One, which represents City of Berkeley workers alongside SEIU 1021.

RETURN TO. Al Austin II, Political and Legislative Director, Al.Austin@ca.afscme57.org

DUE AUGUST 31.

FLAG — question 32 asks whether the candidate is requesting a donation and for what amount. Berkeley's Election Reform Act bars union and PAC contributions entirely and caps every contribution at $60 per donor, so the answer is a legal fact rather than a choice.

Research not yet attached.
